newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers ask for review of CBOT delivery plans.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers ask for review of CBOT delivery plans.

text.p: Lawmakers next week plan to ask the Department of Justice to review the Chicago Board of Trade's plan to change its delivery locations for corn and soybean futures, congressional staff said on Friday.
"The proposal by the CBOT has the potential to severely impede competition and increase market manipulation," a draft letter from the lawmakers to Attorney General Janet Reno said.
The draft was released by the office of Ohio Democratic Rep Marcy Kaptur, who is a moving force behind the letter along with Michigan Democratic Rep John Dingall.
The names of other signatories were not immediately known.
The CBOT plans to establish delivery points along the Illinois river from Pekin, Illinois, to Chicago, including Burns Harbor, Indiana. It eliminates Toledo and St. Louis as delivery points.
"The proposal would result in highly concentrated ownership of delivery elevators among a small number of commercial grain companies along the Illinois River," the letter said.
"Consequently it could increase the possibility of market manipulation at the expense of producers and the corn and soybean industry," it said.
In the letter, the lawmakers asked the Justice Department to make its findings available to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
